intro: Wet rooms have become one of the most sought-after bathroom upgrades across Midlothian, and Arniston is no exception. Whether you're looking to improve accessibility, modernise a dated bathroom, or simply add long-term value to your home, a properly installed wet room delivers on all fronts. The key word there is 'properly' — wet room installation is one of those jobs where cutting corners causes serious, expensive damage. Getting the waterproofing, drainage gradient, and tanking absolutely right from the start is everything. This guide covers what wet room installation in Arniston actually involves, what it costs, and what you need to think about before work begins.
localContext: Arniston's housing stock presents a genuinely varied set of challenges when it comes to wet room installation. The older stone-built properties and period cottages that make up much of the town's character are often working with narrow doorways, uneven original floorboards, and solid stone walls that require careful preparation before any waterproofing can be applied. Solid floors in older homes can be a particular consideration — achieving the correct fall towards the drain sometimes means building up the floor level or recessing the drain, both of which add complexity. On the modern estates in Arniston, the work is typically more straightforward, but suspended timber floors still require a robust tanking system to protect the joists beneath. Arniston sits in a moderately hard water area, which is worth keeping in mind when choosing your shower fittings and screen materials — limescale build-up on exposed surfaces is a real consideration, and many installers will recommend fittings with easy-clean coatings or suggest a scale-reducing shower head to keep maintenance manageable long-term.
serviceDetail: A professional wet room installation in Arniston follows a clear sequence of stages, and understanding them helps you know what to expect and what questions to ask. The process begins with a proper survey of the existing bathroom — checking floor construction, wall condition, existing drainage routes, and the feasibility of achieving the required gradient. This is not a step to rush. For older stone-built properties in Arniston particularly, discovering what's behind the existing tiles or beneath the floorboards early on avoids costly surprises mid-project. Once the survey is complete and a design agreed, the existing bathroom is stripped back to the subfloor and bare walls. The drainage position is set, and if needed, the floor is built up or a pre-formed wet room former is installed to create the correct fall — typically around 1.5% towards the drain. Tanking comes next, and this is the most critical stage. A multi-layer waterproof membrane system is applied across the entire floor and at least 1.8 metres up the walls, with particular care taken at joints and corners where water ingress is most likely. Once the tanking is fully cured, tiling begins — non-slip floor tiles are standard, and the choice of grout should be a waterproof epoxy type for durability. Finally, the shower valve, drain, and any screen or fixed panel are fitted. A good installer will also check that ventilation is adequate, as wet rooms need proper airflow to prevent condensation and damp over time.
pricing: In Arniston, you should realistically budget between £6,500 and £12,000 for a full wet room installation, depending on the complexity of the job and the finish you're after. Older stone-built properties and period cottages tend to sit toward the higher end due to the additional preparation work involved with solid walls, uneven floors, or difficult drainage routes. Modern estate homes with standard bathrooms are more likely to come in toward the lower end of that range. The size of the room, the quality of tiles and fittings chosen, and whether any structural alterations are required all affect the final figure. Accessible wet rooms with features like fold-down seating, grab rails, or level-access for wheelchair users may attract grant funding — worth exploring before you commit to a budget.
whyLocal: Choosing a tradesperson who knows Arniston and the surrounding Midlothian area genuinely matters for a project like this. A local installer will have worked in similar stone-built properties and period cottages before — they won't be surprised by what they find behind the tiles, and they'll know the typical quirks of older construction in this part of Scotland. They're also easier to hold accountable if anything needs attention after completion, and they care about their local reputation. For a wet room — where the waterproofing has to be right first time — experience with the specific property types found in and around Arniston is a real advantage.

faqs.q: Can a wet room be installed in an older stone-built property in Arniston?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely — it just requires more careful preparation. Stone walls need to be checked for moisture and stability before tanking is applied, and solid floors may need the drain position carefully planned to achieve the right fall. An experienced installer will survey the property thoroughly before quoting, so there are no surprises once work begins.

faqs.q: How long does wet room installation typically take in Arniston?
faqs.a: Most wet room projects in Arniston take between five and ten working days from strip-out to completion. Older or more complex properties can take longer, particularly if there's remedial work needed to walls or floors before tanking can start. Your installer should give you a clear programme before work begins so you know what to expect.

faqs.q: Does the moderately hard water in Arniston affect my wet room fittings?
faqs.a: It can over time. Hard water leaves limescale deposits on shower heads, screens, and chrome fittings. Choosing fittings with easy-clean or anti-limescale coatings helps significantly, and a scale-reducing shower head is a worthwhile addition. Regular wiping down of exposed surfaces after use is the simplest way to keep things looking good long-term.

faqs.q: Do I need planning permission for a wet room in Arniston?
faqs.a: In most cases, no — wet room installation is considered permitted development in Scotland. However, if your property is listed or within a conservation area, it's worth checking with Midlothian Council before work starts. Your installer should be able to advise, and any reputable tradesperson will flag this during the initial survey visit.
